_comment: Keys are "<classId>[@<instance>]/<leafId>", because a cascaded property like cooldowntime is
editable on every power and each class needs its own slot. Repeated properties add a
[dimensionKey]; instance-scoped properties on a per-object-config class add @<instance>.
Note both powers' cooldowns are set here. If only the base class had been edited, Singularity
would inherit that edit - and the editor would show it as the effective value, so the user can
see what they will get and override it back if they want.

meta.name: Silver Grind
meta.author: Mgamerz
meta.description: Slower, heavier Silver. Pull actually does something.

_note: One entry per (faction section, instance, difficulty) the user changed - that is how the game stores it: the config section is per INSTANCE, and difficulty is a row INSIDE the enemies array.

The section qualifies the instance because instance names are reused across factions: SFXWave_Horde_Cerberus2's instances carry the base faction's names verbatim, so a key without the section merges two factions' edits into one.

A slot with no counts is the filler - it spends whatever of the wave budget is left. The absence IS the meaning, so the counts are omitted rather than written as null or zero; a zero would leave an ordinary slot that spawns nothing. maxPerWave caps a type's total across the whole wave, as opposed to how many are alive at once.
waveIndex is context, not identity: the instance is what the edit follows. If Milan moves an instance to a different wave, the editor says so rather than repointing the edit.
